Justice delayed - Sharborne Lance killed

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
3 Lives lost, two of them children. A year later and the person responsible has not been brought to book.

Summary:
A 3 car accident results in the deaths of 3 people. Nicola Terblanche/Jameson was driving home from a night at friends, her husband was in the passenger seat and her son - Scott,3, was in the back in a baby car seat. Out of know where a car hits her car. Her foot is broken, she's dazed. Her husband managers to unbuckle his seat belt and get to their son in the back. Unfortunately, Scott died on impact. They go to the hospital and there they find out that the other female driver - Sharborne Lance - and one of the two kids in her car died as well. It's then that Nicola found out that the accident was not caused by this women. In fact, her boyfriend had intentionally hit her and caused her car to his theirs. He fled the scene according to a witness - Mr. Werner du Toit (Mapogo Security). The man accused of this crime is called Elliston "Trompie" Fortuin - he has a murder rap sheet as long as my arms. He's been in and out of jail thrice - serving 18 months, 3 years, 3 years, and 15 years (of which he only served 8) and is currently out on parole from the 15 year sentence. Trompies was arrested at a chop shop trying to get his car fixed after the accident. He was denied bail, however, the charges were provisionally withdrawn (for further investigation) and will be re-instituted soon as the police have escalated the matter to the DPP's office (High Court) because "off the record" there are worries as to the state prosecutor's conduct.

It's a year since the accident and what is taking so long for this to go to court? He's on parole, how can this dangerous man be roaming the streets?

Further information:
I met with the Investigating Officer in the case and his commanding officer. They have told the provincial police that they will allow an interview, but of course it's up to the province. I know the basics of the crash but will obviously back this up with information confirmed from the police.

The witness is willing to speak, as is the family of Sharborne (Father Arthur Lance) and Nicola Jameson. This is a story of a miscarriage of justice. And that will unravel over the next few days depending on what happens with the police file.

The family of Sharborne are willing to speak, they living in the area and will assign someone to speak. The family have the documents that prove Sharborne had a restraining order against Trompies. They broke up and got back together over several years (they began dating in 1999, broke up while he was in jail from 2000-2010, reunited back in 2011, broke up and got back together in 2013, then broke up in March, just before her death.) Sharborne was terrified of him, so much so that she used to check her tracker that was installed in his car, as to his location, and then depending on where he was, she would make sure as to avoid him. He beat her on numerous occasions, and she went to the cops on several occasions. Sharborne fielded several threats from him, and since her death, her family have been the brunt of other threats. I will be able to tell the narration of Trompies as a gangster and abuser through another person appointed by the family. Theirs will be the only identity hidden at this stage. I think it is vital to explain Trompies character.

I think I will ask the correctional services why trompies was given parole and why he has not been re-arrested after he left the accident scene. (I am going to the Boksburg court tomorrow to get the documents entered into court.)

I have asked the department of social development's Minister Bathabile Dlamini for an interview - she is head of the ANC women's league, I would like to ask them about stalking and abuse that results in the death of woman and children. I think it's important as this will create a backbone for a "justice denied" story theme - and more angry voices other than the victims.

Extra Budget Items:
I think we may need to re-enact the accident via graphics and not visuals... I want to do a one day shoot first with the witnesses and family members of all who died and then have a fry session on how we tell the "actual accident" part of this story...
Need to discuss the confront... he is a gangster after all.

Press Release:


Justice Delayed
Just over a year ago a horror crash on Johannesburg’s East Rand tragically claimed the lives of three, including two young children. But was it an accident? Carte Blanche hears evidence and eye witness accounts which may reveal a far more sinister story.




Script:


John Link: “Reiger Park stands at the feet of several mine dumps in Johannesburg’s East Rand. It’s battling massive unemployment, drugs and gangsterism.
Pastor: “In comparison to most of the other coloured area’s Reiger Park is a very small area.”
With over 200 churches Pastor Joseph Booyson says religion is important here. However, gang violence is overpowering the streets he walks.
Pastor: “Unemployment on the backdrop of a turf war, that would come with the smuggling and selling of drugs to the kids and they are being lured into gangsterism, So it’s a more a game of survival.”
Jerome: “In Reigerpark you from the west he from the south, and we call it top and bottom.”
“Jerome,” whose identity has been hidden, is a gangster who was born into this tough environment.
Jerome: The police, some of them drive around just collecting drugs from drug dealers.”
John Question: “It sounds absolutely lawless?”
Jerome: “You can commit a crime today, Monday you can go to court and there’s no case.”
The Lance family has lived here for 4 generations. They are mourning the loss of two family members killed in a mysterious car accident in May last year. The murky details surrounding that night include several unexplained coincidences that HAVE left the survivors of the 3 cars involved with many unanswered questions. 38-year old Sharborne Lance, her son, Shaquille,10, and her nephew Jayden, 12, were in the first car. Only Shaborne’s son, Shaquille survived. Nicola and Danie Terblanche and their son, Scott, were in the second car, and in the 3rd car Sharborne’s ex boyfriend –Elliston Fortuin - better known on the streets as Trompie.
John Link: “According to documents obtained by Carte Blanche from the Boksburg Magistrates court, Trompies claims to have driven into Sharborne’s vehicle because she slammed on her breaks.”
Trompie has a long history with the law and gang violence, and in 2010 he was granted parole from prison after serving a 10-year sentence for various charges which included murder and attempted murder. Since his release, he’s been charged with 3 more crimes, but all of them have been withdrawn. He says Sharborne caused the crash and that this was all just a horrible accident. BUT the evidence may suggest something FAR more sinister.
Octavia: “Sharborne was a very kind person, very compassionate.”
Sharborne’s cousin, Octavia Oliphant, says Sharborne, who was known as “Bona,” and was the family peace-keeper.
Octavia: “She was a single mom for both her kids. I never heard her complain. She bought herself a car and the first cousin in our family that got a drivers license.”
John Question: “How badly is Jayden missed by the family?”
Octavia: “Jayden is the comedian in the family. He was the kind of child that would come to your house and say, Auntie give me a chocolate, or give me money for a chocolate.”
Sharborne’s sister Elzoreen Abdul says the events leading up to their deaths, actually began 16 years prior, when Sharborne began dating Trompie. She says, at first their relationship was a happy one.
Elzoreen: “But then we went out one night, it was in December 1999, when he hited her the first time.
John Question: “When you say hit her?”
Elzoreen: “He beated her, Sharborne was bleeding...the next morning, the way her face looked, was terrible...”
Jerome says Trompie was a quiet boy, until 1995 when he was sucked into gangsterism. His criminal record reveals he was found guilty of the discharge of a firearm and was sentenced to 5 years in jail.
Jerome: “We thought he might have changed by then, while he was out on bail for that case, before he got sentenced, he committed another murder, where he got sentenced to 15 years. And in the event he was out on bail for that one murder, he committed another attempted murder. So basically since 1995 most of the time, until 2010 he was in prison.”
According to the Police, Trompie does have murder and attempted-murder convictions, as well as the possession of an unlicensed firearm with ammunition and the discharge of a firearm conviction.
Elzoreen: “When he came out of jail, he also had someone else, but eventually they ended up together again. Then it started out loving. She did everything a woman could do for a man.”
Until Sharborne called Elzoreen crying.
Elzoreen: “Elzoreen, please come here, Trompie beated me now, saying that I’m after one of his friends.”
Trompie’s alleged jealous rage was a breaking point for Sharborne.
Elzoreen: “She said she needs help. There’s no love in the relationship anymore., He says he’s going to kill both her and her two children.”
Although Sharborne never laid abuse charges against Trompie, she did request an interim restraining order, which was never served on him. After they broke up, Sharborne’s family say she feared for her life.
Less than 10 km from Reigerpark in Boksburgs northern Suburbs, live Nicola and Danie Terblanche who have been married for 11 years. She’s a bookkeeper and he builds specialized car parts for races like the Dakar rally. They couldn’t wait to start a family, and were overjoyed when Nicola had Scott – who, at the time of the accident, was just 3 years old.
Nicola: “He was developing...He was doing so well in school. He just learned new things every day.”
John Link: “It was a Friday night, Nicola and Danie, were making their way home after a night out, their son Scott, was asleep in the backseat of their car.
They were approaching the intersection from that direction, little knowing that from the opposite direction, were a BMW and a polo.
John link: “What happened next would change their lives forever and suggest that this was NO accident.”
Trompie’s car collided with Sharborne’s and the force of the impact caused the BMW to cross over the concrete barrier and into the Yaris head on.
CRASH
Nicola: “Suddenly all I saw was lights, and this car up in the air coming towards me head on, I couldn’t stop.”
Trompie swiftly left the scene of the accident in his blue Polo.
Werner Du Toit, a security patrol officer, witnessed the accident.
John Question: “Were you under the impression that he was trying to get away?”
Werner: “Yes, because if he did it by accident, he was going to stop.”
Caxton East Rand senior journalist Fanie Mthupha happened upon the scene moments after the crash.
Fanie: “ The impact was massive...Blood”
Danie was winded by the airbags and Nicola had broken her ribs and foot. They were desperate to get to their son. Werner stopped to see if he could help Nicola with Scott.
Werner: “I saw he wasn’t breathing anymore.”
John Question: “So what did you say to her?”
Werner: “I didn’t tell her anything, because I didn’t know what to say.”
Nicola: “I knew already, as a mother, and as a father, my husband knew.”
Scott was pronounced brain dead at the hospital...
Fanie: “In this particular accident, when I saw the children, I almost cried myself.”
John Question: “The astonishing thing, is reading about the accident in the early reports, it almost sounds like a two car accident?
Nicola: “I thought this woman had just lost control, maybe she was drunk, or I don’t know, but I was very angry.”
Nicola: “Only I think the next day did we hear from the police that this man was following her and deliberately pushed her off the road and into us.”
On the night of the accident Trompie said he called Sharborne several times, and then saw her drive past him and so he made a u-turn in an attempt to speak to her. He said, “I increased my speed so as to catch up with her, the deceased slammed on brakes...I did not stop at the scene of the accident and drove away. I was highly traumatized and shocked... After the accident Trompie said: “I took my motor vehicle to Eldorado Park in an attempt to repair it and that is where the SAPS found and arrested me. I have no sensible reason as to why I acted in this manner...”
According to the police, Trompie was charged with culpable homicide. He was denied bail, but was then unexpectedly released, because the police wanted to investigate further. They have since obtained cell phone records, an accident report and the tracker location details from the vehicles. It’s now the NPA’s decision to re-instate the original charge or change it to a charge of murder.
John Link: Whether this is a case of murder or just a tragic accident will be for a court to decide, for now though, the case has been provisionally withdrawn for further investigation, leaving both families to wonder, when Trompie’s day in court will come.”
We called Trompie, he says he stands by his affidavit.
“My version of events never will change hey, because that was the truth.”
We asked about his relationship with Sharborne.
“We met nearly 20 years ago man. We were in good terms hey.”
He declined an interview initially, but then said he would consider it.
“For the mere fact that I’m out on parole for a murder case.”
“Let me first consult my lawyer, then I’ll get back to you hey.”
Trompie has ignored all our subsequent requests for an interview and has not responded to our written questions.
The Lance family have their doubts about Trompie’s version of events as Sharborne was allegedly using his car’s tracker system to avoid seeing him. Jerome says his threats against the family to withdraw from the investigation, since her death, are cause for the gangs to take the situation into their own hands, if the case is not re-instated soon.
Jerome: “He threatened that Sharborne’s father would actually bury one of his children every week.”
John: “Why do you think she chose a gangster?”
Octavia: “ The broblem with Sharborne...She thought maybe she’ll be able to change him.”
The lance family say they keep the Terblanche’s in their prayers. Fanie says the East Rand seems plagued by unsolved cold cases.
Fanie: “I’m not just pointing fingers at the police, it looks like they’ve failed to solve the problem for a long time.”
Nicola: “There are 1000’s of people like me, whose cases will never see the light of day.”
The Terblanche’s say they were just in the wrong place at the wrong time.
Nicola: “Every night you expect him to come around the children... and it’s hard.”
Almost a year to the day, and Trompie is still walking the streets of Reiger Park. The case against him is hanging in the balance waiting for the wheels of the justice system to turn. Both the NPA and the police have declined interviews, but ALL the families want are answers. Nicola says she may never get closure over Scott’s senseless death.
Nicola: “You know he would have grown into a good man... He was a very special little boy.”

Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 29 May 2016 - Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 03 June 2016 Press Release: Justice Delayed Just over a year ago a horror crash on Johannesburg’s East Rand tragically claimed the lives of three, including two young children. But was it an accident? Carte Blanche hears evidence and eye witness accounts which may reveal a far more sinister story. Script: John Link: “Reiger Park stands at the feet of several mine dumps in Johannesburg’s East Rand. It’s battling massive unemployment, drugs and gangsterism. Pastor: “In comparison to most of the other coloured area’s Reiger Park is a very small area.” With over 200 churches Pastor Joseph Booyson says religion is important here. However, gang violence is overpowering the streets he walks. Pastor: “Unemployment on the backdrop of a turf war, that would come with the smuggling and selling of drugs to the kids and they are being lured into gangsterism, So it’s a more a game of survival.” Jerome: “In Reigerpark you from the west he from the south, and we call it top and bottom.” “Jerome,” whose identity has been hidden, is a gangster who was born into this tough environment. Jerome: The police, some of them drive around just collecting drugs from drug dealers.” John Question: “It sounds absolutely lawless?” Jerome: “You can commit a crime today, Monday you can go to court and there’s no case.” The Lance family has lived here for 4 generations. They are mourning the loss of two family members killed in a mysterious car accident in May last year. The murky details surrounding that night include several unexplained coincidences that HAVE left the survivors of the 3 cars involved with many unanswered questions. 38-year old Sharborne Lance, her son, Shaquille,10, and her nephew Jayden, 12, were in the first car. Only Shaborne’s son, Shaquille survived. Nicola and Danie Terblanche and their son, Scott, were in the second car, and in the 3rd car Sharborne’s ex boyfriend –Elliston Fortuin - better known on the streets as Trompie. John Link: “According to documents obtained by Carte Blanche from the Boksburg Magistrates court, Trompies claims to have driven into Sharborne’s vehicle because she slammed on her breaks.” Trompie has a long history with the law and gang violence, and in 2010 he was granted parole from prison after serving a 10-year sentence for various charges which included murder and attempted murder. Since his release, he’s been charged with 3 more crimes, but all of them have been withdrawn. He says Sharborne caused the crash and that this was all just a horrible accident. BUT the evidence may suggest something FAR more sinister. Octavia: “Sharborne was a very kind person, very compassionate.” Sharborne’s cousin, Octavia Oliphant, says Sharborne, who was known as “Bona,” and was the family peace-keeper. Octavia: “She was a single mom for both her kids. I never heard her complain. She bought herself a car and the first cousin in our family that got a drivers license.” John Question: “How badly is Jayden missed by the family?” Octavia: “Jayden is the comedian in the family. He was the kind of child that would come to your house and say, Auntie give me a chocolate, or give me money for a chocolate.” Sharborne’s sister Elzoreen Abdul says the events leading up to their deaths, actually began 16 years prior, when Sharborne began dating Trompie. She says, at first their relationship was a happy one. Elzoreen: “But then we went out one night, it was in December 1999, when he hited her the first time. John Question: “When you say hit her?” Elzoreen: “He beated her, Sharborne was bleeding...the next morning, the way her face looked, was terrible...” Jerome says Trompie was a quiet boy, until 1995 when he was sucked into gangsterism. His criminal record reveals he was found guilty of the discharge of a firearm and was sentenced to 5 years in jail. Jerome: “We thought he might have changed by then, while he was out on bail for that case, before he got sentenced, he committed another murder, where he got sentenced to 15 years. And in the event he was out on bail for that one murder, he committed another attempted murder. So basically since 1995 most of the time, until 2010 he was in prison.” According to the Police, Trompie does have murder and attempted-murder convictions, as well as the possession of an unlicensed firearm with ammunition and the discharge of a firearm conviction. Elzoreen: “When he came out of jail, he also had someone else, but eventually they ended up together again. Then it started out loving. She did everything a woman could do for a man.” Until Sharborne called Elzoreen crying. Elzoreen: “Elzoreen, please come here, Trompie beated me now, saying that I’m after one of his friends.” Trompie’s alleged jealous rage was a breaking point for Sharborne. Elzoreen: “She said she needs help. There’s no love in the relationship anymore., He says he’s going to kill both her and her two children.” Although Sharborne never laid abuse charges against Trompie, she did request an interim restraining order, which was never served on him. After they broke up, Sharborne’s family say she feared for her life. Less than 10 km from Reigerpark in Boksburgs northern Suburbs, live Nicola and Danie Terblanche who have been married for 11 years. She’s a bookkeeper and he builds specialized car parts for races like the Dakar rally. They couldn’t wait to start a family, and were overjoyed when Nicola had Scott – who, at the time of the accident, was just 3 years old. Nicola: “He was developing...He was doing so well in school. He just learned new things every day.” John Link: “It was a Friday night, Nicola and Danie, were making their way home after a night out, their son Scott, was asleep in the backseat of their car. They were approaching the intersection from that direction, little knowing that from the opposite direction, were a BMW and a polo. John link: “What happened next would change their lives forever and suggest that this was NO accident.” Trompie’s car collided with Sharborne’s and the force of the impact caused the BMW to cross over the concrete barrier and into the Yaris head on. CRASH Nicola: “Suddenly all I saw was lights, and this car up in the air coming towards me head on, I couldn’t stop.” Trompie swiftly left the scene of the accident in his blue Polo. Werner Du Toit, a security patrol officer, witnessed the accident. John Question: “Were you under the impression that he was trying to get away?” Werner: “Yes, because if he did it by accident, he was going to stop.” Caxton East Rand senior journalist Fanie Mthupha happened upon the scene moments after the crash. Fanie: “ The impact was massive...Blood” Danie was winded by the airbags and Nicola had broken her ribs and foot. They were desperate to get to their son. Werner stopped to see if he could help Nicola with Scott. Werner: “I saw he wasn’t breathing anymore.” John Question: “So what did you say to her?” Werner: “I didn’t tell her anything, because I didn’t know what to say.” Nicola: “I knew already, as a mother, and as a father, my husband knew.” Scott was pronounced brain dead at the hospital... Fanie: “In this particular accident, when I saw the children, I almost cried myself.” John Question: “The astonishing thing, is reading about the accident in the early reports, it almost sounds like a two car accident? Nicola: “I thought this woman had just lost control, maybe she was drunk, or I don’t know, but I was very angry.” Nicola: “Only I think the next day did we hear from the police that this man was following her and deliberately pushed her off the road and into us.” On the night of the accident Trompie said he called Sharborne several times, and then saw her drive past him and so he made a u-turn in an attempt to speak to her. He said, “I increased my speed so as to catch up with her, the deceased slammed on brakes...I did not stop at the scene of the accident and drove away. I was highly traumatized and shocked... After the accident Trompie said: “I took my motor vehicle to Eldorado Park in an attempt to repair it and that is where the SAPS found and arrested me. I have no sensible reason as to why I acted in this manner...” According to the police, Trompie was charged with culpable homicide. He was denied bail, but was then unexpectedly released, because the police wanted to investigate further. They have since obtained cell phone records, an accident report and the tracker location details from the vehicles. It’s now the NPA’s decision to re-instate the original charge or change it to a charge of murder. John Link: Whether this is a case of murder or just a tragic accident will be for a court to decide, for now though, the case has been provisionally withdrawn for further investigation, leaving both families to wonder, when Trompie’s day in court will come.” We called Trompie, he says he stands by his affidavit. “My version of events never will change hey, because that was the truth.” We asked about his relationship with Sharborne. “We met nearly 20 years ago man. We were in good terms hey.” He declined an interview initially, but then said he would consider it. “For the mere fact that I’m out on parole for a murder case.” “Let me first consult my lawyer, then I’ll get back to you hey.” Trompie has ignored all our subsequent requests for an interview and has not responded to our written questions. The Lance family have their doubts about Trompie’s version of events as Sharborne was allegedly using his car’s tracker system to avoid seeing him. Jerome says his threats against the family to withdraw from the investigation, since her death, are cause for the gangs to take the situation into their own hands, if the case is not re-instated soon. Jerome: “He threatened that Sharborne’s father would actually bury one of his children every week.” John: “Why do you think she chose a gangster?” Octavia: “ The broblem with Sharborne...She thought maybe she’ll be able to change him.” The lance family say they keep the Terblanche’s in their prayers. Fanie says the East Rand seems plagued by unsolved cold cases. Fanie: “I’m not just pointing fingers at the police, it looks like they’ve failed to solve the problem for a long time.” Nicola: “There are 1000’s of people like me, whose cases will never see the light of day.” The Terblanche’s say they were just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Nicola: “Every night you expect him to come around the children... and it’s hard.” Almost a year to the day, and Trompie is still walking the streets of Reiger Park. The case against him is hanging in the balance waiting for the wheels of the justice system to turn. Both the NPA and the police have declined interviews, but ALL the families want are answers. Nicola says she may never get closure over Scott’s senseless death. Nicola: “You know he would have grown into a good man... He was a very special little boy.”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): 3 Lives lost, two of them children. A year later and the person responsible has not been brought to book.
metadata.Summary: A 3 car accident results in the deaths of 3 people. Nicola Terblanche/Jameson was driving home from a night at friends, her husband was in the passenger seat and her son - Scott,3, was in the back in a baby car seat. Out of know where a car hits her car. Her foot is broken, she's dazed. Her husband managers to unbuckle his seat belt and get to their son in the back. Unfortunately, Scott died on impact. They go to the hospital and there they find out that the other female driver - Sharborne Lance - and one of the two kids in her car died as well. It's then that Nicola found out that the accident was not caused by this women. In fact, her boyfriend had intentionally hit her and caused her car to his theirs. He fled the scene according to a witness - Mr. Werner du Toit (Mapogo Security). The man accused of this crime is called Elliston "Trompie" Fortuin - he has a murder rap sheet as long as my arms. He's been in and out of jail thrice - serving 18 months, 3 years, 3 years, and 15 years (of which he only served 8) and is currently out on parole from the 15 year sentence. Trompies was arrested at a chop shop trying to get his car fixed after the accident. He was denied bail, however, the charges were provisionally withdrawn (for further investigation) and will be re-instituted soon as the police have escalated the matter to the DPP's office (High Court) because "off the record" there are worries as to the state prosecutor's conduct. It's a year since the accident and what is taking so long for this to go to court? He's on parole, how can this dangerous man be roaming the streets?
metadata.Further information: I met with the Investigating Officer in the case and his commanding officer. They have told the provincial police that they will allow an interview, but of course it's up to the province. I know the basics of the crash but will obviously back this up with information confirmed from the police. The witness is willing to speak, as is the family of Sharborne (Father Arthur Lance) and Nicola Jameson. This is a story of a miscarriage of justice. And that will unravel over the next few days depending on what happens with the police file. The family of Sharborne are willing to speak, they living in the area and will assign someone to speak. The family have the documents that prove Sharborne had a restraining order against Trompies. They broke up and got back together over several years (they began dating in 1999, broke up while he was in jail from 2000-2010, reunited back in 2011, broke up and got back together in 2013, then broke up in March, just before her death.) Sharborne was terrified of him, so much so that she used to check her tracker that was installed in his car, as to his location, and then depending on where he was, she would make sure as to avoid him. He beat her on numerous occasions, and she went to the cops on several occasions. Sharborne fielded several threats from him, and since her death, her family have been the brunt of other threats. I will be able to tell the narration of Trompies as a gangster and abuser through another person appointed by the family. Theirs will be the only identity hidden at this stage. I think it is vital to explain Trompies character. I think I will ask the correctional services why trompies was given parole and why he has not been re-arrested after he left the accident scene. (I am going to the Boksburg court tomorrow to get the documents entered into court.) I have asked the department of social development's Minister Bathabile Dlamini for an interview - she is head of the ANC women's league, I would like to ask them about stalking and abuse that results in the death of woman and children. I think it's important as this will create a backbone for a "justice denied" story theme - and more angry voices other than the victims.

I want to do a one day shoot first with the witnesses and family members of all who died and then have a fry session on how we tell the "actual accident" part of this story... Need to discuss the confront... he is a gangster after all.
